title: On the uniqueness of the strictly convex quadrilateral central configuration with a fixed angle

predicted_errors.error_location: Lemma 2, displayed formula for a0 = zeta5*zeta6
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The 2x2 block for (r12,r34) is [[R12, 2 eta cos theta], [2 eta cos theta, R34]], so its characteristic polynomial is zeta^2 - (R12+R34) zeta + (R12 R34 - 4 eta^2 cos^2 theta). Thus a0 = zeta5 zeta6 must be R12 R34 - 4 eta^2 cos^2 theta. The paper instead writes a0 = 4 r12^3 r13^6 r14^6 r23^6 r24^6 r34^3 (R12 R34 - 4 eta^2 r12^3 r34^3 cos^2 theta), which is not the determinant of that block.

predicted_errors.error_location: Lemma 2, equations expressing cos theta from the critical equations
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: From (18), S12 = m1 m2 r12 (delta - r12^{-3}), so -S12/(2 eta r34) = m1 m2 r12 (r12^{-3} - delta)/(2 eta r34). Equivalently S12/r12 = m1 m2(delta - r12^{-3}) = R12 - 3 m1 m2 / r12^3, not R12 - 3/r12^3. The paper omits the mass factors m1 m2 (and m3 m4 in the analogous r34 expression).

predicted_errors.error_location: Lemma 2, final expression for a0 after substitution
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Using the correct relations gives a0 = 3 m1 m2 m3 m4 [(r12 r34)^{-3} + delta (r12^{-3} + r34^{-3})], not a0 = 3 m1 m2 m3 m4 (1 + (r12^3 + r34^3) delta). The printed formula is algebraically wrong and dimensionally inconsistent.
The text says D1 'forms a quarter of a disk with radius 1/2', but D1 is defined by 0 <= r14^2 + r23^2 = G1 <= 1/2. Hence the radius is 1/sqrt(2), not 1/2.
The text defines H = {(r12, r34) in (R+)^2 | r12^2 + r34^2 <= 1} but then says 'Now fix a point (r14, r23) in H'. It should fix a point (r12, r34) in H; as written the variables are mismatched.

predicted_errors.error_location: Lemma 3, cos theta != 0 case, WLOG assumption w1 <= 0
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof assumes 'Without loss of generality, w1 = r12 - r34 <= 0'. This restricts the domain to configurations with r12 <= r34, but the full M0^+ contains both signs of w1. No symmetry or gluing argument is supplied to justify that the restricted set has the same contractibility/Euler characteristic as the full set.
